messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: mixed parameter/data matrices and arrays
parts:
With the new design for agrad we're looking at, there's
the opportunity to mix parameters (stan::agrad::var)
and data (double) into a single matrix, vector, or array.

(Alas, this still won't let us do missing data a la
BUGS with NA entries.)

The issue is whether we need to do one check for is-var
or one for each item of each array. For instance,
here's the way I implemented dot product:

inline var dot(Eigen::Matrix<var,1,Eigen::Dynamic>& a,
Eigen::Matrix<var,1,Eigen::Dynamic>& b) {
if (a.size() != b.size())
throw std::domain_error("vectors a and b must be same size in
dot product");
if (a.size() == 0)
return var(0);

double val(0.0);
for (int i = 0; i < a.size(); ++i)
val += a(i).val_ * b(i).val_;
int node = alloc_node();
for (int i = 0; i < a.size(); ++i) {
if (a(i).is_var()) // ########################
set_next_edge(a(i).node_, b(i).val_);
if (b(i).is_var()) // ########################
set_next_edge(b(i).node_, a(i).val_);
}
return var(val, node);
}

The tests on the lines with the "#" signs are pretty
expensive (the routine's about 10% faster w/o them).
The is_var method itself is a simple lookup that gets
inlined (same speed calling function as brute-force unfolding).

We only need to do those tests once if the arrays are
all homogeneous.

The only place this comes into play is in missing data
problems where a parameter is half missing data and half
known data. In the current Stan implementation, the
known data gets promoted to a var and everything's the same
type.

- Bob
